name: dev.edgegap/mcp
title: Edgegap
description: Deploy and operate multiplayer game servers on Edgegap's global edge network.

tools.name: edgegap_context
tools.description: Report which Edgegap API this server talks to, its version, whether it is the local or hosted server, and the guardrails in force: read-only mode, application allowlist, max_duration ceiling, the agent deployment cap, the tag forced onto every deployment, and which tools support dry_run. Also gives the egress terms per hosting type, the API rate limits and webhook rules for backend code, and says whether this session has a usable token and, if not, why and how to fix it. Call it first when unsure what this session is allowed to do, before anything billable, or when tool calls fail with a token problem. Makes no API call unless check_token is true, and never shows the token.

check_token.description: Make one read-only API call (list one application) to confirm Edgegap accepts the token. Default false.

tools.name: edgegap_list_apps
tools.description: List the applications in the Edgegap organization. Start here before creating or deploying anything, so you reuse an existing application instead of making a duplicate. An "application" groups versions of one game server.

tools.name: edgegap_create_app
tools.description: Create a new application to hold game server versions. Only call this after edgegap_list_apps confirms no suitable application exists. Creating an application does not deploy anything — follow with edgegap_create_app_version.

name.description: Application name, 3-64 chars. Usually the game or project name.

is_active.description: Whether deployments are allowed. Default true.

dry_run.description: Show the exact request (method, host, path, body) with secrets masked, and send nothing. Local checks still run. Use it to confirm a billable or destructive call before making it.

tools.name: edgegap_update_app
tools.description: Set whether an application accepts new deployments. Turning it off stops new deployments of every version under it; running deployments keep running. Use it to pause an application without deleting anything.

is_active.description: false blocks new deployments; true allows them again.

dry_run.description: Show the exact request (method, host, path, body) with secrets masked, and send nothing. Local checks still run. Use it to confirm a billable or destructive call before making it.

tools.name: edgegap_list_app_versions
tools.description: List the versions under an application, with their container image, resources, ports (including whether TLS Upgrade is on, which browser/WebGL clients need for wss://) and whether a registry login is set for pulling the image. Use this to find the version name to deploy, to check a version is ready before deploying, or to copy the non-secret settings (image, resources, ports) of a working version when creating a new one. The registry login and secret env values are never readable: the API returns "This value is set and encrypted" for them, so get them from the dashboard's Container Registry page or the developer.

application.description: Application name, as returned by edgegap_list_apps. Required; without it the applications are listed.

tools.name: edgegap_get_app_version
tools.description: Read one version in full: image, resources, ports, max_duration, whether image caching (force_cache) and verify_image are on, restart policy, the Endpoint Storage its logs go to, and the names of its env vars (values are never shown). Use it before edgegap_update_app_version or edgegap_deploy to check what a version will do.

application.description: Application name. Required; without it the applications are listed.

version.description: Version name, as listed by edgegap_list_app_versions. Required; without it the versions are listed.

tools.name: edgegap_create_app_version
tools.description: Register a container image as a deployable version of an application. The image must already be pushed to a registry that Edgegap can pull from (see edgegap_get_registry_credentials and edgegap_list_registry_tags). Resource units: 1024 cpu units = 1 vCPU; memory_mb must be at least 256 and at most double the cpu units. Set verify_image true on the first version so a bad image fails here rather than at deploy time. Refused, with nothing sent, for the "latest" or an empty docker tag (use a build ID so deployments are reproducible) and for a docker_image that also holds a registry host or tag. Env vars named like secrets (TOKEN, SECRET, PASSWORD, API_KEY…) are hidden in the dashboard. Images on registry.edgegap.com need no registry login: leave registry_username and registry_token out and the version gets the organization's own registry login (registry_profile "Edgegap"). When copying an existing version, copy only non-secret settings: the API returns "This value is set and encrypted" for its registry login and secret env values, and that placeholder is refused here.

name.description: Version identifier, typically a build ID or timestamp.

docker_tag.description: Image tag: a build ID, commit SHA or timestamp. "latest" and empty tags are refused.

memory_mb.description: Memory in MB. At most 2x cpu_units.

protocol.description: One of UDP, TCP, TCP/UDP, HTTP, HTTPS, WS, WSS. Most game servers use UDP.

to_check.description: Readiness check on this port. Default true.

tls_upgrade.description: Edgegap terminates TLS on this port, so clients connect with wss:// or https://. Required for browser (WebGL) clients, which cannot use plain ws:// from an https page. WS and HTTP ports only. Default false.

ports.description: Ports to expose. At least one is required for players to connect.

registry_username.description: Registry username, for private images on other registries (Docker Hub, GHCR, ECR...). Leave it out for registry.edgegap.com: Edgegap then pulls with the organization's own registry login (registry_profile "Edgegap").

max_duration_minutes.description: Auto-stop after this many minutes. Keeps test deployments from running up cost.

restart_policy.description: What Edgegap does when the server process exits. "never" for match servers that stop themselves (an exit or crash ends the deployment instead of restarting a half-played match); "on_failure" restarts only after a crash (persistent servers); "always" (the API default) restarts after any exit.

verify_image.description: Verify Edgegap can pull the image before accepting the version.

endpoint_storage.description: Endpoint Storage name (edgegap_list_endpoint_storage) to export container logs to when deployments end.

env.description: Environment variables injected into the container. Values are never echoed back.

dry_run.description: Show the exact request (method, host, path, body) with secrets masked, and send nothing. Local checks still run. Use it to confirm a billable or destructive call before making it.

tools.name: edgegap_update_app_version
tools.description: Change settings on an existing version instead of creating a new one: point it at a new image tag, turn it on or off, change max_duration, set the registry login (the API cannot add registry_profile "Edgegap" to an existing version: create a new version for that), turn on image caching (force_cache: Edgegap pre-loads the image so deployments start faster), set the restart policy, or set the shutdown grace period. Only the fields you pass change. Deployments already running keep their old settings; new deployments get the new ones. Same refusals as edgegap_create_app_version: "latest" or empty tags, a docker_image holding a host or tag, and the API token in the registry login or env vars. ports and env REPLACE the version's whole list (per the API): read the current ones with edgegap_get_app_version and pass every port or variable to keep; secret env values are not readable, so get them from the developer. Refused, with nothing sent, for a registry login or env value equal to the API's "This value is set and encrypted" placeholder; leave the registry login out to keep it. cpu_units and memory_mb change together (both or neither); to try other resources for one deployment only, override them in edgegap_deploy instead.

is_active.description: false blocks new deployments of this version.

docker_tag.description: New image tag: a build ID, commit SHA or timestamp.

registry_token.description: Registry password or token. Never echoed back.

max_duration_minutes.description: Auto-stop after this many minutes. Capped by EDGEGAP_MAX_DURATION_MINUTES.

cpu_units.description: New vCPU units for later deployments, with memory_mb. 1024 = 1 vCPU.

memory_mb.description: New memory in MB for later deployments, with cpu_units. At most 2x cpu_units.

force_cache.description: Pre-load the image on Edgegap so deployments start faster.

verify_image.description: Check Edgegap can pull the image when saving.

endpoint_storage.description: Endpoint Storage name (edgegap_list_endpoint_storage) to export container logs to when deployments end.

restart_policy.description: What Edgegap does when the server process exits. "never" for match servers that stop themselves (an exit or crash ends the deployment instead of restarting a half-played match); "on_failure" restarts only after a crash (persistent servers); "always" (the API default) restarts after any exit.

termination_grace_period_seconds.description: Seconds between SIGTERM and SIGKILL when a deployment stops.

ports.description: REPLACES every port on the version. Include the ports to keep, not only new ones.

protocol.description: One of UDP, TCP, TCP/UDP, HTTP, HTTPS, WS, WSS. Most game servers use UDP.

to_check.description: Readiness check on this port. Default true.

tls_upgrade.description: wss:// / https:// for browser clients. WS and HTTP ports only.

env.description: REPLACES every env var on the version; [] removes them all. Values are never echoed back.

dry_run.description: Show the exact request (method, host, path, body) with secrets masked, and send nothing. Local checks still run. Use it to confirm a billable or destructive call before making it.

tools.name: edgegap_list_locations
tools.description: List the cities Edgegap can deploy to. Pass application and version to see only the locations with capacity for that version right now. Use it to pick geo_coordinates for edgegap_deploy when you have no player IPs, or to tell a developer where their players can be served from. For the ping beacons game clients use to measure latency, see edgegap_list_ping_beacons.

application.description: With version: only locations with capacity for it now.

tools.name: edgegap_list_ping_beacons
tools.description: List Edgegap's ping beacons: one host per region that a game client can ping (UDP or TCP) to measure its latency before matchmaking. The matchmaker's latency rules use these measurements. Read-only; the game client does the pinging, not this tool.

tools.name: edgegap_deploy
tools.description: Start one authoritative dedicated game server from an application version, placed near the players you specify. The server owns the game state, so no player hosts it. Returns immediately with a request_id; the server is still starting and has no connection details yet. Follow this call with edgegap_wait_for_deployment to get the address players connect to. Always stop deployments you started for testing. Every deployment is tagged "edgegap-mcp" in addition to any tags you pass, so edgegap_list_deployments with only_agent_deployments: true finds them all. Runs until stopped or until the version's max_duration, which the result reports. Refused, with nothing sent, if the API token appears in an env var or tag, if the version uses the "latest" docker tag, or when too many agent deployments are already running (EDGEGAP_MAX_AGENT_DEPLOYMENTS, default 5): stop finished ones first. Also refused when the version's max_duration is unlimited or above EDGEGAP_MAX_DURATION_MINUTES, unless allow_long_running is true (ask the developer first), and on the local server after EDGEGAP_MAX_DEPLOYS_PER_RUN deploys (default 20). Env vars named like secrets are hidden in the dashboard. Optional: webhooks Edgegap calls when the server is ready, errors or ends, require_cached_locations for faster starts, and private_host_ids to place it on your private fleet first. Backend code that deploys (POST /v2/deployments, 40/s per organization) should track servers with these webhooks, not by polling status (20/s for the whole organization); webhooks are not retried or signed, so keep polling as a fallback only.

ip_addresses.description: Public IPv4/IPv6 addresses of the players. Edgegap places the server near them.

geo_coordinates.description: Latitude/longitude pairs, as an alternative to IP addresses.

users.description: Where the players are. Exactly one of these two is required.

env.description: Environment variables for this deployment only. Values are never echoed back.

tags.description: Extra tags for filtering later, e.g. ["agent-test"]. "edgegap-mcp" is always added.

cpu_units.description: Override the version's CPU for this deployment only, with memory_mb. 1024 = 1 vCPU.

memory_mb.description: Override the version's memory for this deployment only, with cpu_units. At most 2x cpu_units.

require_cached_locations.description: Only place it where the image is already cached: starts faster, fewer places to choose from. Needs force_cache on the version (edgegap_update_app_version); without it the API refuses the deploy.

webhook_on_ready.description: https URL Edgegap POSTs to when the container started (the engine may still be loading). Sent once, not retried, not signed.

webhook_on_error.description: https URL Edgegap POSTs to when the deployment fails. Sent once, not retried, not signed.

webhook_on_terminated.description: https URL Edgegap POSTs to when the deployment ends. Sent once, not retried, not signed.

private_host_ids.description: Private fleet host IDs to try first, in order (from edgegap_list_fleet_hosts); Edgegap overflows to its cloud when they are full. Omit for a normal cloud deployment.

allow_long_running.description: Deploy even though the version's max_duration is unlimited or above EDGEGAP_MAX_DURATION_MINUTES. Only after the developer agreed: the server bills until it is stopped or that limit.

dry_run.description: Show the exact request (method, host, path, body) with secrets masked, and send nothing. Local checks still run. Use it to confirm a billable or destructive call before making it.

tools.name: edgegap_get_deployment
tools.description: Read the current status of one deployment, including connection address and ports once it is ready. For a deployment you just created, prefer edgegap_wait_for_deployment — it polls for you instead of making you call this in a loop. This is GET /v1/status, limited to 20 requests/s for the whole organization (shared with Context): backend code should use deployment webhooks and poll only as a fallback.

tools.name: edgegap_wait_for_deployment
tools.description: Poll a deployment until it is ready, errors, or the timeout expires, then return the connection details. This is the tool to call right after edgegap_deploy. Do not build your own polling loop — this handles backoff and reports the container error detail if the server fails to start. For backend code that tracks many deployments, use deployment webhooks instead: status polling is limited for the whole organization.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait before giving up, 5-600. Default 180.

tools.name: edgegap_list_deployments
tools.description: List active deployments, optionally filtered and sorted. Use this to find deployments left running from earlier sessions before starting new ones — orphaned servers cost money. Backend code: the list API is limited to 10 requests/s per organization, so reconcile on a schedule, not per match. Filter by status, application, version, tags, request_id, created_at, fleet_name or host_name, e.g. [{field:"application",operator:"eq",value:"my-game"},{field:"status",operator:"eq",value:"ready"}]. Operators: eq and neq on every field except created_at (eq, gte, lte); in and nin with an array value on request_id, tags, application, version, fleet_name, host_name; ilike with % wildcards on fleet_name and host_name. At most one filter per field. Sort by created_at or available_session_sockets. To find every deployment an agent started through this server, pass only_agent_deployments: true (the same as filtering tags in ["edgegap-mcp", "mcp"]).

only_agent_deployments.description: Only deployments started through this server: tagged "edgegap-mcp", or "mcp" by versions up to 0.3.3. Cannot be combined with a tags filter.

value.description: A string, or an array of strings for in/nin. created_at is ISO 8601, e.g. "2026-09-30T00:00:00Z".

tools.name: edgegap_stop_deployment
tools.description: Gracefully stop one deployment by request_id, sending SIGTERM to the container. Stop every deployment you started for testing before ending your task. This tool stops exactly one deployment, named by its exact request_id: empty IDs, wildcards and lists are refused, and bulk stop is deliberately not exposed. A deployment this server started (tagged "edgegap-mcp") stops right away; any other running deployment may be serving players, so without confirm: true the result only previews it and nothing is sent.

request_id.description: The exact request_id of the one deployment to stop, e.g. "61b1be8f54d9".

confirm.description: Set true only after the developer approved this exact call. Without it nothing is sent: the result previews what would be stopped or deleted (status "confirmation_required").

dry_run.description: Show the exact request (method, host, path, body) with secrets masked, and send nothing. Local checks still run. Use it to confirm a billable or destructive call before making it.

tools.name: edgegap_get_deployment_logs
tools.description: Retrieve stdout/stderr and crash output for a deployment. Call this whenever a deployment errors or a server exits unexpectedly — the crash exit code usually identifies the problem faster than redeploying does. Logs for stopped deployments are only retained if Endpoint Storage was configured on the version beforehand.

max_characters.description: Truncate logs to this length (500-50000), keeping the tail. Default 8000.

tools.name: edgegap_get_deployment_metrics
tools.description: Summarise a deployment's resource use over time: CPU, CPU throttling, memory and network, each as latest, average, p95 and peak, with the API's own labels, plus anomaly flags (spikes above mean + 3 sd, a rising trend such as a memory leak, any CPU throttling) collected in `anomalies`. Use it to size a version (cpu_units, memory_mb) from a real match, or to check whether a crash was memory or CPU starvation before redeploying. Defaults to the whole life of the deployment. To compare two versions, use edgegap_compare_versions.

start_time.description: ISO 8601. Default: when the deployment started.

end_time.description: ISO 8601. Default: now, or when it stopped.

step.description: Averaging step, e.g. "30s" or "5m". Default: the API's.

tools.name: edgegap_fleet_health
tools.description: One call for "is anything wrong right now?" across running deployments, instead of checking them one by one: counts by status, the deployments in error with their error detail, ones stuck starting for over 10 minutes, and totals per location and per version with unhealthy ones flagged. check_crashes: true also reads each deployment's crash data (restarts, exit codes). Covers what Edgegap still lists: stopped deployments are gone, so this is current state, not history. Inspects up to 20 deployments per call, newest first. Read-only. Next: edgegap_search_deployment_logs for what the errors say, edgegap_compare_versions for a rollback decision.

check_crashes.description: Also read crash data (restart count, exit code) per deployment. Default false.

tools.name: edgegap_search_deployment_logs
tools.description: Search the container and crash logs of running deployments of an application (and version) for a pattern, and group the matching lines by error, with counts and which deployments printed them: "every crash in version 1.4.2 since yesterday, grouped by error". Without a pattern it looks for errors, exceptions, fatal signals and out-of-memory kills. Also counts crash exit codes. Logs only exist while a deployment runs (or in Endpoint Storage), so stopped deployments are not searched. Searches up to 20 deployments per call, newest first. Read-only.

pattern.description: Text to find, case-insensitive. Default: common error and crash words.

regex.description: Treat pattern as a regular expression. Default false.

started_after.description: Only deployments started after this ISO 8601 time, e.g. "2026-11-12T00:00:00Z" for the last day.

max_groups.description: Most error groups to return, 1-50. Default 15.

tools.name: edgegap_compare_versions
tools.description: Compare two versions of one application from their running deployments, to back a rollback or promote decision: deployments in error, crash restarts and exit codes, and CPU and memory (average, p95, peak) against each version's requested cpu_units and memory_mb, with the differences spelled out. Reads up to 6 running deployments per version, newest first, so both versions need deployments running now (stopped ones keep no logs or status). Read-only.

version_a.description: The baseline version, e.g. the one in production.

version_b.description: The version to compare against it, e.g. the new build.

tools.name: edgegap_generate_dockerfile
tools.description: Write a Dockerfile for this project's headless game server build, ready for Edgegap: linux/amd64 base, the build folder copied in, the binary made executable, the right headless flags (Unity -batchmode -nographics, Godot --headless), a non-root user where the engine needs it (Unreal refuses root), CRLF fixes for start scripts, and EXPOSE lines matching the ports. Call this when the project has no Dockerfile, before building anything. Look at the build output first so you can pass the real build folder, binary name and port; anything you omit is assumed and listed under assumptions, which you must confirm with the developer or the project files. Write the result to Dockerfile, then build. The output is checked against edgegap_validate_server_config before it is returned. Makes no API calls.

engine.description: Game engine of the server build.

build_path.description: Server build folder, relative to where docker build runs. Defaults: unity "Builds/EdgegapServer", unreal "." (run from inside the packaged LinuxServer folder), godot "build".

executable.description: File name of the server binary or start script inside build_path. Defaults: unity "ServerBuild", unreal "StartServer.sh", godot "server.x86_64". Required for "other".

ports.description: Ports the server listens on. Default: 7777, with the protocol the netcode uses (UDP if unknown).

tls_upgrade.description: TLS Upgrade (wss/https) on a WS or HTTP port, for browser clients.

netcode.description: Networking transport, to pick the protocol. Known: mirror-kcp, kcp, mirror-telepathy, telepathy, mirror-simpleweb, simpleweb, websocket, fishnet-tugboat, tugboat, netcode-for-gameobjects, ngo, unity-transport, utp, photon-fusion, litenetlib, enet, unreal-netdriver, godot-enet, godot-websocket.

launch_args.description: Extra server arguments, one per entry, e.g. ["-log", "-port=7777"].

tools.name: edgegap_validate_server_config
tools.description: Check a game server Dockerfile and the ports/resources you intend to register against what Edgegap requires, BEFORE building and pushing. Catches the failures that otherwise only show up after a build, push, version and deploy: ARM or Windows images (Edgegap runs linux/amd64), Unreal running as root, missing Unity -batchmode -nographics, a server bound to localhost, EXPOSE ports that do not match the version ports, a protocol that does not match the netcode transport, the "latest" tag, and bad CPU/memory ratios. Pass the Dockerfile text (read it from disk first). If there is no Dockerfile yet, call edgegap_generate_dockerfile instead. Makes no API calls.

engine.description: Game engine. Detected from the Dockerfile when omitted.

netcode.description: Networking transport, to check the port protocol. Known: mirror-kcp, kcp, mirror-telepathy, telepathy, mirror-simpleweb, simpleweb, websocket, fishnet-tugboat, tugboat, netcode-for-gameobjects, ngo, unity-transport, utp, photon-fusion, litenetlib, enet, unreal-netdriver, godot-enet, godot-websocket.

ports.description: Ports you plan to pass to edgegap_create_app_version.

tls_upgrade.description: TLS Upgrade (wss/https) on a WS or HTTP port, for browser clients.

tools.name: edgegap_get_registry_credentials
tools.description: Get the push login for this organization's private Edgegap container registry (registry.edgegap.com) and the exact docker login, build and push commands for your image. Use this when the server image is not in a registry yet. Edgegap only hands these credentials to the quick-start token the Unity/Unreal plugins use; with a regular API token or Edgegap sign-in this tool cannot fetch them and instead returns the steps to copy them from the dashboard's Container Registry page — ask the developer for them then, do not retry. When it does return a token, it is registry-scoped (push/pull images in this project), not the org API token: pass it to docker login via --password-stdin, never as a command-line argument, and do not write it into files. Call edgegap_validate_server_config before building. Any other registry Edgegap can pull from (Docker Hub, GHCR, ECR, GitLab) works too: then skip this tool and pass that registry and its pull login to edgegap_create_app_version.

image_name.description: Image name without project or tag, e.g. "my-game-server". Used to build the commands.

tag.description: Unique build tag for the commands, e.g. a build ID. Never "latest".

tools.name: edgegap_list_registry_tags
tools.description: List the tags pushed for one image in this organization's Edgegap container registry, with push time and size. Call it after docker push to confirm the tag landed before edgegap_create_app_version, which otherwise fails later with an image-pull error. An image that was never pushed comes back as status "not_found" with no tags, not as an error. Only for registry.edgegap.com: images in Docker Hub, GHCR or another registry are not listed here.

image_name.description: The image name only, without the project, registry host or tag, e.g. "my-game-server". The API reads the project from your token; "<project>/my-game-server" is not found.

tools.name: edgegap_delete_registry_tag
tools.description: Delete one tag, and the image it points to, from this organization's Edgegap container registry, to clean up old builds. Takes exactly one image name and one exact tag; wildcards, lists and "latest" are refused, and there is no bulk delete. A version that still uses the tag can no longer start deployments, so check edgegap_list_app_versions first. Cannot be undone, so without confirm: true the result only previews it and nothing is sent.

image_name.description: The image name only, e.g. "my-game-server", as for edgegap_list_registry_tags.

tag.description: The exact tag to delete, e.g. "build-41".

confirm.description: Set true only after the developer approved this exact call. Without it nothing is sent: the result previews what would be stopped or deleted (status "confirmation_required").

dry_run.description: Show the exact request (method, host, path, body) with secrets masked, and send nothing. Local checks still run. Use it to confirm a billable or destructive call before making it.

tools.name: edgegap_tag_deployment
tools.description: Add tags to, or remove tags from, one running deployment, e.g. to mark the match it serves or that a test is done, so edgegap_list_deployments can filter on them. Tags are labels only: the game server does not see the change. The "edgegap-mcp" tag cannot be removed, since it is how agent deployments are found and cleaned up. Returns the tags now on the deployment.

request_id.description: The exact request_id of the deployment.

add.description: Tags to add, at most 40 characters each.

dry_run.description: Show the exact request (method, host, path, body) with secrets masked, and send nothing. Local checks still run. Use it to confirm a billable or destructive call before making it.

tools.name: edgegap_report_deployment
tools.description: Report a problem with one deployment to Edgegap (the API's "Report a Deployment", meant for a studio's moderation backend), with a short reason and optional key/value details. It does not stop the deployment. Use it only when the developer asks to report a deployment; for a crash, read edgegap_get_deployment_logs first.

request_id.description: The exact request_id of the deployment.

dry_run.description: Show the exact request (method, host, path, body) with secrets masked, and send nothing. Local checks still run. Use it to confirm a billable or destructive call before making it.

tools.name: edgegap_delete_app_version
tools.description: Delete one version of an application, to clean up test versions. Exactly one exact version name; refused while any deployment of that version is running. The container image stays in the registry (edgegap_delete_registry_tag removes it). Cannot be undone, so without confirm: true the result only previews it and nothing is sent.

version.description: The exact version name to delete.

confirm.description: Set true only after the developer approved this exact call. Without it nothing is sent: the result previews what would be stopped or deleted (status "confirmation_required").

dry_run.description: Show the exact request (method, host, path, body) with secrets masked, and send nothing. Local checks still run. Use it to confirm a billable or destructive call before making it.

tools.name: edgegap_delete_app
tools.description: Delete one application and every version under it, to clean up a test application. Exactly one exact name; refused while any of its deployments is running, and refused when it has more versions than max_versions (default 0: delete its versions first with edgegap_delete_app_version, or raise max_versions after the developer agreed). Registry images are not touched. Cannot be undone, so without confirm: true the result only previews it and nothing is sent.

application.description: The exact application name to delete.

confirm.description: Set true only after the developer approved this exact call. Without it nothing is sent: the result previews what would be stopped or deleted (status "confirmation_required").

max_versions.description: Delete only if it has at most this many versions. Default 0.

dry_run.description: Show the exact request (method, host, path, body) with secrets masked, and send nothing. Local checks still run. Use it to confirm a billable or destructive call before making it.

tools.name: edgegap_list_fleet_hosts
tools.description: List the hosts in one of the organization's private fleets (dedicated machines Edgegap manages for you), with status, IP and location. Only ACTIVE hosts accept deployments. Pass their host_id values to edgegap_deploy as private_host_ids to place a server on them first. edgegap_context gives the egress terms for fleet hosts and cloud overflow. Organizations without private fleets get an error from the API.

fleet_name.description: The private fleet name, as shown in the dashboard.

tools.name: edgegap_list_endpoint_storage
tools.description: List the organization's Endpoint Storage: S3-compatible buckets Edgegap exports container logs to when a deployment ends (so logs survive the deployment), and the pull profiles under each, which copy files from the bucket into a container at boot. Secret keys are never returned. A version uses a storage for logs through edgegap_create_app_version / edgegap_update_app_version endpoint_storage, and a pull profile through edgegap_link_pull_profile.

tools.name: edgegap_create_endpoint_storage
tools.description: Register an S3-compatible bucket (AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, DigitalOcean Spaces, ...) as Endpoint Storage, so container logs are exported there when deployments end. The developer supplies the bucket, endpoint URL and an access key pair scoped to that bucket; never invent or reuse other credentials, and never pass the Edgegap API token. The secret key is sent once and never echoed back. Then set endpoint_storage on the version (edgegap_update_app_version) to turn log export on.

endpoint.description: https URL of the S3 endpoint, without the bucket, e.g. "https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com".

access_key_id.description: Access key ID for the bucket.

secret_access_key.description: Secret access key for the bucket. Never echoed back.

container_log_version.description: v1 (default) writes one file per deployment; v2 streams chunks while it runs.

dry_run.description: Show the exact request (method, host, path, body) with secrets masked, and send nothing. Local checks still run. Use it to confirm a billable or destructive call before making it.

tools.name: edgegap_create_pull_profile
tools.description: Create a pull profile under an Endpoint Storage: at boot, Edgegap copies a file or folder from the bucket into the container (maps, configs, large assets kept out of the image). It does nothing until linked to a version with edgegap_link_pull_profile. Avoid destination paths the image already uses.

source.description: Path in the bucket, starting with "/" and without a trailing "/", e.g. "/maps" or "/config/server.json". Letters, digits, "_", "-", "+" and "." only.

source_type.description: Whether source is a file or a folder.

destination.description: Absolute path in the container, e.g. "/data/maps".

dry_run.description: Show the exact request (method, host, path, body) with secrets masked, and send nothing. Local checks still run. Use it to confirm a billable or destructive call before making it.

tools.name: edgegap_link_pull_profile
tools.description: Link a pull profile to an application version, so its new deployments get the bucket files at boot, or unlink it (unlink: true). Running deployments are not changed.

dry_run.description: Show the exact request (method, host, path, body) with secrets masked, and send nothing. Local checks still run. Use it to confirm a billable or destructive call before making it.

tools.name: edgegap_delete_pull_profile
tools.description: Delete one pull profile from an Endpoint Storage, to clean up a test profile. Exactly one exact name. Every version linked to it stops getting its files at boot (the API cannot list those links, so ask the developer when the profile is not one this conversation created). The bucket and its files are not touched. Cannot be undone.

pull_profile.description: The exact pull profile name to delete.

dry_run.description: Show the exact request (method, host, path, body) with secrets masked, and send nothing. Local checks still run. Use it to confirm a billable or destructive call before making it.

tools.name: edgegap_delete_endpoint_storage
tools.description: Delete one Endpoint Storage, to clean up a test one. Exactly one exact name; refused when it still has more pull profiles than max_pull_profiles (default 0: delete them first with edgegap_delete_pull_profile, or raise max_pull_profiles after the developer agreed). Versions that export logs to it stop doing so, so confirm with the developer when the storage is not one this conversation created. The bucket and the logs already in it are not touched. Cannot be undone.

endpoint_storage.description: The exact Endpoint Storage name to delete.

max_pull_profiles.description: Delete only if it has at most this many pull profiles, which go with it. Default 0.

dry_run.description: Show the exact request (method, host, path, body) with secrets masked, and send nothing. Local checks still run. Use it to confirm a billable or destructive call before making it.

tools.name: edgegap_build_matchmaker_config
tools.description: Generate a ready-to-upload Edgegap matchmaker JSON configuration with one profile: team count and size, optional latency rule, and optional expansions that relax the rules the longer a player waits. Checks the referenced application version exists and has ports. Edgegap has no API for creating a matchmaker, so this tool does NOT create one: save the returned config to a file (e.g. matchmaker-config.json) and have the developer upload it on the Matchmaker page of the dashboard. The matchmaker starts one dedicated server for each match.

profile_name.description: Profile clients will queue into, e.g. "casual-2v2".

team_count.description: Teams per match. 1 for free-for-all or co-op.

max_latency_ms.description: Adds a latency rule: drop players above this ping to the chosen region. Needs beacon pings from the client.

latency_difference_ms.description: Max ping spread between matched players. Default 100.

expansions.description: Rule relaxations after a player has waited this long, e.g. [{after_seconds: 20, min_team_size: 1}]. Keep each below ticket_expiration. Not needed for partial matches: min_team_size below max_team_size already allows them. Expansions cost the matchmaker performance, so add one only to relax a rule.

ticket_expiration.description: Default "30s", so a developer testing alone is matched or told to retry within 30 s instead of waiting minutes. Raise it only for production queues.

inspect.description: Expose the inspection API for debugging. Default true; turn off for production.

verify_version.description: Look up the application version first. Default true.

allowed_cors_origins.description: Origins of web pages allowed to call the matchmaker, e.g. ["https://mygame.example.com", "http://localhost:8080"]. Required when game clients run in a browser (WebGL): browsers block matchmaker calls from any origin not listed. Scheme and host only, no path.

tools.name: edgegap_list_skills
tools.description: List the Edgegap agent skills: tested, step-by-step workflows for getting a multiplayer game online on Edgegap, with templates (Dockerfiles, matchmaker configs, Unity C# and Unreal C++ drop-ins) and known pitfalls. Each entry says which engine, netcode or backend it is for, and the server instructions map projects to skills. edgegap_get_skill returns the text of a skill; "edgegap" covers any other engine and points to the rest. Also says whether a newer skills pack is on GitHub (reads one version number, no Edgegap API call).

tools.name: edgegap_get_skill
tools.description: Load one Edgegap agent skill: its SKILL.md (the workflow to follow) by default, or one of its reference documents or templates with file. edgegap_list_skills and the server instructions say which skill fits which project ("edgegap" covers any other engine). No API call.

skill.description: Skill name, from edgegap_list_skills: edgegap, edgegap-browser-wasm, edgegap-chat-canvas, edgegap-cocos, edgegap-colyseus, edgegap-containerize, edgegap-deployments-api, edgegap-eos-voice, edgegap-fal, edgegap-fishnet, edgegap-fusion, edgegap-fusion-simplefps, edgegap-godot, edgegap-launch, edgegap-local-testing, edgegap-manus, edgegap-matchmaking, edgegap-nakama, edgegap-ngo, edgegap-playfab, edgegap-purrnet, edgegap-relays, edgegap-samples, edgegap-server-design, edgegap-supabase, edgegap-threejs, edgegap-troubleshoot, edgegap-ugs-matchmaker, edgegap-unity, edgegap-unreal, edgegap-vibe-coded. Required; without it the skills are listed.

file.description: A file inside the skill, e.g. "references/deploy.md" or "assets/docker/Dockerfile". Default SKILL.md.

tools.name: edgegap_update_skills
tools.description: Check whether the Edgegap agent skills installed in the developer's agent are the latest, and update them. This hosted server cannot see the developer's disk: pass installed_versions (each loaded skill's metadata.version from its SKILL.md frontmatter) and it compares them with the latest on GitHub and says how to update. Skill text is never downloaded by this tool. The skills served by edgegap_get_skill need no update here.

installed_versions.description: Skill name → version of skills you have loaded from somewhere this server cannot see, e.g. {"edgegap-unity": "0.1.8"}. The version is metadata.version in the SKILL.md frontmatter.
